title: Midnight Menagerie
headline: All four builders back. Attacker animates, hover at 33ms, pets have faces, the route reads as a route.

pieces.name: Engine foundation
pieces.desc: Renderer, scene manager, clock, RNG, save, dev server, asset pipeline

pieces.name: Combat engine
pieces.desc: Turn rules, damage pipeline, statuses, intents, deterministic + headless
pieces.verdict: 649 assertions. Trackers install at combat start, counters declare their own states, intents carry addsCards and rule.

pieces.name: Card feel
pieces.desc: Hover, drag, arc-fan hand, play arc, impact, re-fan easing
pieces.verdict: Hover 168ms to 33ms event-to-settled, lift 116px to 45-54px, scale 1.180x. Hand spreads: zero text occlusions at 3 and 5 cards. Aiming card held at z700 with 0 cards over it.

pieces.name: Combat presentation
pieces.desc: Battlefield staging, enemy rigs, damage numbers, hit reactions, VFX
pieces.verdict: Attacker displacement 0px to 90px, per silhouette family. The player has a body. Chooser cancels. Intent prints the real Clutter count.

pieces.name: Enemies & intents
pieces.desc: Rosters, move selection, telegraph clarity, Scuffles and Big Scares
pieces.verdict: 12 new behavioural Haunt upgrades from the design doc, all Courage-neutral. New opening formation halves free openings from 26% to 15.5%.

pieces.name: Blueprint routes
pieces.desc: Branching route map drawn on the mansion blueprint sections
pieces.verdict: Route redrawn as graphite over print: warm, continuous, curved, double-passed with a relief stroke. Row 11 now one Safe Room plus real alternatives across 85 sheets.

pieces.name: Companion decks
pieces.desc: Card pools + keyword systems for the 16 Companions
pieces.verdict: Haunt now deals damage (0 ticks in 300 fights, now 261 ticks / 424 Courage). Ignores Guard now pierces.

pieces.name: Run layer
pieces.desc: Rewards, shops, rest, Curiosities, Keepsakes, Backpack
pieces.verdict: Two-region runs validated: whole-run survival 50%, Governess 73.7% when reached, boss 9.4 turns. Courage floor on wing entry.

pieces.name: Title / Select / Clubhouse
pieces.desc: Front end, Companion select, investigation board
pieces.verdict: Eight pets and eight kids are real generated photographs with eyeshine, flash falloff and date imprints. Fresh save reads 0/16 freed.

pieces.name: Audio
pieces.verdict: 46 synthesised SFX cues + 10-track adaptive music. 0 errors, no clipping, 61fps.

pieces.name: Atmosphere
pieces.desc: Lighting, fog, post FX, dust, candle flicker, transitions
pieces.verdict: 61fps on every scene at 1600x900 and 1920x1080, with the look metrics improved: mid-tones 24.9%, median luma 38.6, cross-correlation 0.30.

pieces.name: UI chrome & clarity
pieces.desc: HUD, tooltips, deck views, settings, previews, accessibility
pieces.verdict: One HUD across six scenes, Snacks usable, deck viewable everywhere, Settings reachable, 27 checks 0 errors.

events.msg: Project scaffolded: Three.js engine, asset pipeline, dev server, design doc carved into 45 reference files.
Design doc carved into 45 reference files under docs/design/.
Data schemas locked (game/src/data/schema.js) so six agents can build in parallel.
Slay the Spire 2 reference yardstick written to docs/STS2-REFERENCE.md - every critic judges against it.
Wave 1 launched: 6 builders in parallel - combat engine, card feel, companion decks, enemies, atmosphere, audio, blueprint map.
Front-end builder started on Title, Companion Select, Clubhouse and Expedition End.
Session rate limit hit mid-wave; five builders resumed from their partial work rather than restarted.
All eight Wave 1 builders running: combat engine, card feel, companion decks, enemies, atmosphere, audio, blueprint map, front-end.
Combat engine complete: 10 modules, 13 statuses, 48 keywords, 261 passing assertions. Two real bugs caught by its own suite.
Combat presentation builder started - the screen where the game is actually played.
Enemies done: 37 defs, 137 moves, 3 multi-phase bosses, dynamic intents verified in both directions.
Audio done: 46 hand-synthesised cues, soundtrack analysed and cue-mapped by spectral centroid, loop points measured.
Critics dispatched on card feel and on game design (cards + enemies + balance simulation).
Card pools done: 445 cards, 54 companion keywords, validated against the live engine.
Terminology corrected to the design doc: energy is Nerve (not Pluck), currency is Lost Things.
Terminology swept across 15 files: Nerve, Courage, Guard, Tricks, Keepsakes, Lost Things.
Critics running on card feel and on game design. Front-end finisher building the Expedition End screen.
CRITIC FAIL on enemies: multi-hit attacks deal hits-squared damage. Proven by A/B - fixing it takes an elite from 0% to 72.5% win rate.
Combat engine PASSES round 2: 445 assertions, real player choice, intent queue, House Rules.
CRITIC FAIL on card feel. Hover (100ms), arc, re-fan and keyboard all tied with StS2 - but the hand does not fit the screen and the targeting arrowhead is a zero-area path.
Design critic also flagged 9 near-duplicate card groups and two byte-identical cards at different rarities.

Card pools round 2: the duplicate detector was keyed on rarity, so 'same card one rarity up' passed by construction. Detector rewritten around effect shape; it independently found the same nine groups the critic did.
Combat screen playable end to end: procedural enemy rigs, intent shields, Nerve orb, draw and discard piles.
CRITIC FAIL on map: setPointerCapture makes every node unclickable. Three clicks changed one pixel.
CRITIC FAIL on atmosphere: measured mid-tones 12.3% vs the reference art's 24.1%; 17 regions are one room recoloured (structural correlation 0.737).
Combat presentation shipped: intents with redundant shape+glyph channels, honest '6?' previews for unmade choices, 61fps.
Enemies round 2: the hits-squared bug is fixed and pinned by a test that resolves all 65 attack moves and asserts damage equals intent.
Enemy agent's insight: its test mock implemented the mechanic it was testing, so the bug passed forever. A mock that implements a mechanic cannot prove it exists.
Front-end complete: Expedition End built from scratch with a snuffed candle and a real card-view ledger; Select's deck preview was silently broken and is now real cards.
Run layer started - the missing connective tissue. Nothing had built state/run.js, so every screen was mocking the run.
Combat engine PASSES round 3: 478 assertions. announceRule now replaces by source, which is what silently broke the Butler.
UI chrome builder started: the keyword tooltip system, run HUD, deck viewer, settings, and a colourblind-safe palette.
Atmosphere root cause found: 9 of 11 materials were raw ShaderMaterial, which ignores Three.js lights entirely. Lighting now lands on surfaces.
Map round 2 verified by direct DOM probe: clicking works, the walked path inks, branching nearly doubled (34 nodes to 64).
Card feel round 2: the contrast failure was structural - the card face was a child of the frame, so the unplayable filter dimmed the text. Face is now a sibling.
Run layer, Keepsakes and Curiosities now exist on disk. UI chrome building the keyword tooltip system.
Run layer complete - the game is now playable end to end: title, select, map, combat, reward, shop, rest, Curiosity, expedition end.
PERFORMANCE ALERT: measured on the real Intel GPU (not software), the title screen runs at 15fps and combat at 35fps. Automatic fail; dedicated perf pass starting.
Map round 2: the entrance stall was 115 simultaneous SVG dash animations forcing a full re-raster. Replaced with one composited sweep; worst frame gap 2564ms to 149ms.
Tooling fix: shot.py's js: step was awaiting returned promises, so motion strips all landed on the end state. That had already fooled one review.
Full-game playthrough started: one fresh agent playing a complete expedition, a second run, and a quit-and-resume.
PERFORMANCE FIXED: every scene 61fps at both resolutions, up from 15-47. Frame time 24.1ms to 14.0ms; at 1080p 46.5ms to 17.5ms.
Biggest single win was invisible to pass profiling: instanced attributes marked dirty every frame on STATIC_DRAW buffers, stalling the D3D11 driver.

PLAYTHROUGH VERDICT: each module passes its own harness and silently no-ops at the join. Haunt dealt no damage; 'Ignores Guard' did not; the shared HUD is imported by zero scenes; 8 scenes call audio with the wrong id separator.
Root cause was my own instruction: I told every agent to guard cross-system calls with '?.', which turned missing implementations into silent no-ops. CONTRACTS.md rewritten.
Seam checker found 103 problems, not the 3 reported. Fixed 96. Empowered added zero damage; play-dead threw on its first line; five statuses were never registered.
Critical: Companion statuses were never registered in the balance simulation, so every prior Marmalade balance number is suspect. Re-measuring.
Balance pass started - the first that can measure a build where the mechanics actually work. The simulator itself is being rebuilt to play whole regions with real decks.
Shared HUD adopted across six scenes; Snacks are usable at last; Settings reachable during a run; the title's bespoke overlay and combat's bespoke modal both deleted.
Google Fonts was holding page load for 5.8s, delaying first render and skewing every timing measurement. Fonts now vendored locally (195KB).
SEAM CLASS CLOSED: 1556 call sites checked, 0 problems. A dev-only strict Proxy now throws on any undefined ctx or hook member.
Engine round 4: the state cache dirty flag was a boolean cleared at the end of the build, so mutations raised mid-snapshot were swallowed. Now a revision counter.
Combat scene and run layer both in round 2: intent tooltips, per-room backdrops, a boss arena, and the mid-combat resume exploit.
Balance: the simulator was rebuilt to play whole regions with real decks, upgrades, Keepsakes and Snacks, driven by a beam-search bot that scores by simulating the enemy turn.
Boss win rate 20% to 60% for a competent player; boss length 16 turns to 12.6. Region survival 36.7% to 46.7%, short by exactly one Safe Room.
Two more inert mechanics found: the Butler's Roughhousing rule could never fire, and Lost Luggage's deck interference adds nothing in a real run.
Engine round 5: the dead-counter bug had a twin sitting next to it. damageTakenThisTurn was also never written, and livesSpentThisTurn could never have worked.
Boss now has its own arena: Receiving Chamber, distinct palette, the Butler large and centred.
Resume exploit closed: rooms are now entered on the way in and cleared only when they resolve. Replay verified against a board digest before it is trusted.
Notes split into one file per agent: two agents had lost sections to concurrent writes on the shared file.
Combat scene round 2: the intent tooltip was printing escaped HTML as visible text and dismissing itself on the first pixel of movement - a shared-tooltip API trap, now documented in the file.
Fight opening was animating behind the transition veil because scenes await enter() before revealing. 1781ms of black screen before the first card; now ~1000ms.
Map round 3: the blueprint architecture was drawn at alpha 0.74, competing with the route on equal terms. Dropped to 0.52 - that, not line weight, is what made the route readable.
Target contradiction found: region survival 60-75% and boss win 45-65% are mutually exclusive, since survival is roughly P(reach) x P(win boss). Revising.
BALANCE IN BAND: region survival 70%, boss 82.5%, Scuffles 3.9 turns costing 10.6 Courage. The naive-to-competent gap is 33.3 points, so decisions genuinely matter.
Haunt scaling had no continuous axis: hpMul was applied once at level 1 and never again, so Haunt 20 fielded the same Courage as Haunt 1.
Loose ends cleared across seven owners. Found in passing: every card was playing the skill sound, because the two card:play emitters carried different payloads.
Second full playthrough started - an independent cold read, deliberately not shown the first report.
Enemy round 3: the test suite had never executed a single Haunt branch - every section built enemies at Haunt 0. New sweep runs all 37 enemies across 814 Haunt combinations.
That new sweep immediately caught a silent no-op in the agent's own new code: a buff-strip calling a method that does not exist, behind a typeof guard.
Extending runs to two regions. The Nursery and The Governess are authored and validated but the simulator stopped at the first boss, so they have never been played.
Two regions validated and kept: whole-run survival 50%, The Governess 73.7% when reached. The Nursery had been authored at first-region power against a deck 60% bigger with 5x the Keepsakes.
PLAYTHROUGH: 7 dimensions to StS2, 3 ties, 2 wins (atmosphere and accessibility). Zero console errors across two full runs - rare and worth protecting.
The p2 softlock was settled as NOT a softlock: every exit works, but Escape's refusal message is painted 160 z-layers beneath the modal that provoked it.
Render seam closed. Also caught: retained cards were wiped at end of turn with nothing putting them back.
Card feel round 3: the hand host was a full-screen pointer-events layer. Fixed generically, which also fixed the showcase harness's identical bug that nobody had noticed.
Cinzel draws 1 as a Roman I, so the Nerve orb and every counter read as letters. Numerals moved off it and lining figures now inherit globally.
Run-end 'played 21x' was an invented statistic - literally 4 + rng.int(38). No per-card play count exists, so it now reports something true.
A backtick inside a template literal has taken the whole app down twice. Documented with six other traps in CONTRACTS.md.
Fourth blind playthrough started, deliberately not told what was fixed.

BIGGEST GAP FOUND AND FIXED: a CSS class collision. The Curiosity scene and the Safe Room both declared .rs-door; stylesheets are global and never unload, so visiting one Curiosity permanently deleted every Safe Room for the rest of the run - all healing and all card upgrading, with zero console output.
That single bug explains why the simulator (which models rests working) disagreed with actual play. A run's own summary said SAFE ROOMS 0 after walking through two.
New gate: tests/scene-css/check.py fails the build if two scenes declare the same class with conflicting layout. Now at 0 conflicts.
Map round 4: rounds 2 and 3 both measured an improvement to route visibility and neither could work - route and building were the same kind of mark, so weight was the only free variable.
That round also found 149 rooms across 85 sheets whose every exit was a Big Scare. The earlier 'all elites avoidable' rule was only a global property, not a local one.
Card feel round 4: the 116px hover lift was a real bug - the card anchors at its bottom centre, so a 1.19x scale added the whole 0.19x height on top of the 46px lift.
Silhouette coverage was worse than reported: 286 of 429 cards fell through to a 4-shape fallback pool. Now 0 unmatched.

Combat juice: the pose was applied inside an SVG viewBox that fits into a 170px stage, so a full lunge was worth 12 on-screen pixels - and it was spring-chased, so it never arrived. Now explicit ramps in screen pixels.
petKind in schema.js was invented during scaffolding and wrong for five of eight pets. Orbit was listed as a parrot; the design doc says he is a black cat with a white chest patch.
